items.title: Inertial and piecewise inertial worldlines of the affine Minkowski model
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $I$ be an order-convex subset of
$\mathbb{R}$ with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]), and let curves
$x:I\to A$ and their derivatives be as in
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]: the displacement
$x(s+h)-x(s)$ is taken in the affine structure of
[[def-affine-space-and-displacement]], and $x'(s)\in V$, when it exists, is the
limit of the difference quotients, read in the coordinate calculus of
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]] in any inertial chart
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]],
[[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]).

### (a) Inertial worldlines

A curve $x:I\to A$ is **inertial** (also called **uniform** or **straight**)
when there are a parameter value $s_0\in I$, an event $p\in A$ and a vector
$d\in V$, with $d$ future timelike
([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), such that

$$x(s)=p+(s-s_0)\,d\qquad\text{for every }s\in I.$$

The affine action is defined for every real parameter and every vector, so the
display defines a map $I\to A$
([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]); its image is
$x[I]=\{p+\lambda d:\lambda=s-s_0,\ s\in I\}$, and a restriction of an inertial
worldline to a subinterval of $I$ is inertial with the same $d$. Its tangent is
the constant vector $d$: in the chart $x_A$ of an inertial frame the coordinate
path is the affine function $s\mapsto x_A(p)+(s-s_0)E^{-1}(d)$, whose difference
quotients equal the constant $E^{-1}(d)$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]), so $x'(s)=d$ at
every $s\in I$ by the difference-quotient definition in
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]; the same computation gives
$C^k$ regularity for every $k\ge1$. Since the constant tangent $d$ is future
timelike by hypothesis, an inertial curve is a future timelike worldline of the
model ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (Worldlines)). If two inertial worldlines
$x(s)=p+(s-s_0)d$ and $y(t)=p'+(t-t_0)d'$ have the same image and the same
direction of traversal, that is $d'=\alpha d$ with $\alpha>0$, then $p'$ lies in
the image of $x$, so $p'=p+\mu d$ for some real $\mu$, and

$$y(t)=x\bigl(s_0+\mu+\alpha(t-t_0)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }t\text{ in the domain of }y,$$

an increasing affine reparametrization. Here an **increasing affine reparametrization** means
composition with a bijection of parameter domains of the form
$t\mapsto\alpha t+\beta$ with $\alpha>0$. Conversely, composing an inertial
worldline with such a bijection gives an inertial worldline with the same image. This
computation uses only the affine axioms and $d\ne0$.

### (b) Piecewise inertial worldlines

Let $a<b$ be real numbers with $[a,b]\subseteq I$. A curve $x:[a,b]\to A$ is
**piecewise inertial** when there are a finite partition
$a=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_m=b$, events $p_1,\dots,p_m\in A$ and future timelike vectors
$d_1,\dots,d_m\in V$ such that

$$x(s)=p_i+(s-s_{i-1})\,d_i\qquad\text{for every }s\in[s_{i-1},s_i]\text{ and every }i=1,\dots,m,$$

and consecutive pieces agree at the partition points, that is
$p_{i+1}=p_i+(s_i-s_{i-1})d_i=x(s_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,m-1$. The joining condition
makes the piecewise formulas define a single function on $[a,b]$, whose tangent
on each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ is the constant $d_i$ and whose finite
one-sided difference-quotient tangents at an interior partition point $s_i$ are
$d_i$ from the left and $d_{i+1}$ from the right; at the endpoints $a$ and $b$
the one-sided quotients are $d_1$ and $d_m$. Hence a piecewise inertial curve is
a piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline on $[a,b]$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] — no continuous extension of the
derivative to the closed pieces is required, and the tangents are future timelike
at every smooth point and on both sides of every corner — and it is
$C^1$ on $[a,b]$ if and only if $d_1=d_2=\dots=d_m$. The events $x(s_i)$ with
$0<i<m$ are the **corners** of the itinerary, and the itinerary is a **two-leg
itinerary** when $m=2$.

### (c) Scope

The definition asserts the existence of no worldlines beyond the explicitly
parametrized straight and piecewise straight ones, and it attaches no clock
reading to any curve: readings of ideal clocks are the subject of the model's
postulates, not of this definition. No choice principle is used, since every
object is finitely parametrized and every operation is finite-dimensional.
items.strategy: A definition item: it fixes the model's inertial and piecewise inertial vocabulary and makes no proof claim beyond well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the affine formula x(s) = p + (s - s_0) d is a well-defined map I -> A because the affine action of def-affine-space-and-displacement is defined for every real parameter and every vector; (ii) its derivative is the constant d: in the chart x_A of an inertial frame the coordinate path is the affine function s |-> x_A(p) + (s - s_0) E^{-1}(d), whose difference quotients are the constant E^{-1}(d) (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis), so x'(s) = d by def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline (a); the same computation gives C^k regularity for every k; (iii) future timelikeness of the constant tangent is part of the hypothesis, so x is a worldline and not merely a curve; (iv) in (b) the joining condition makes the piecewise formulas define one function on [a,b], and the one-sided derivatives at the corners exist by the two constant formulas; the equivalence with C^1 is immediate because the derivative is constant on each open piece; (v) clause (c) records the interface with the proper-time and endpoint-bound items of this pair. No choice principle is used: the objects are finitely parametrized and every operation is finite-dimensional.

items.title: The reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for future timelike vectors
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and let v,w in V be future timelike vectors. Put a := sqrt(-eta(v,v)) > 0 and b := sqrt(-eta(w,w)) > 0, the timelike lengths of v and w. Then: (i) -eta(v,w) >= a b > 0; (ii) equality -eta(v,w) = a b holds if and only if v and w are positive proportional, that is w = t v for some real t > 0 or v = t w for some real t > 0; (iii) consequently -eta(v,w) > a b whenever v and w are not positive proportional, and eta(v,w) < 0 in every case; (iv) for two past timelike vectors v,w the same inequality -eta(v,w) >= sqrt(-eta(v,v)) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) holds, with equality if and only if they are positive proportional, because -v and -w are future timelike and eta(-v,-w) = eta(v,w). The statement uses only eta and the future cone C^+ and involves no chart, frame or choice principle.
items.strategy: Proof strategy, in an arbitrary inertial frame. Fix an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) (lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist, def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart) and write v = v^0 e_0 + v_s, w = w^0 e_0 + w_s with v_s,w_s in the spatial three-space S. Future timelikeness of v and w is, in these coordinates, v^0 > |v_s| and w^0 > |w_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components, whose coordinate description applies because e_0 is future). Bilinearity gives -eta(v,w) = v^0 w^0 - delta(v_s,w_s) where delta is the Euclidean form on S (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame), and the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite) gives delta(v_s,w_s) <= |v_s| |w_s|, so -eta(v,w) >= v^0 w^0 - |v_s| |w_s|. The algebraic identity (v^0 w^0 - |v_s||w_s|)^2 - ((v^0)^2 - |v_s|^2)((w^0)^2 - |w_s|^2) = (v^0 |w_s| - w^0 |v_s|)^2, together with a = sqrt((v^0)^2 - |v_s|^2) and b = sqrt((w^0)^2 - |w_s|^2) (def-rational-power, thm-of-square-roots), shows that v^0 w^0 - |v_s| |w_s| is a nonnegative real whose square dominates (ab)^2; monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives (lem-of-square-monotone) gives (i). For (ii), equality in the two-step estimate forces both delta(v_s,w_s) = |v_s||w_s| and v^0 |w_s| = w^0 |v_s|. The equality case of the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite) makes v_s and w_s nonnegatively proportional; if one of them is 0 then the second equality forces the other to be 0 as well and v,w are positive multiples of e_0; otherwise v_s = t w_s with t > 0 and v^0 |w_s| = w^0 t |w_s| gives v^0 = t w^0, hence v = t w. The converse is a direct substitution: eta(t w, w) = t eta(w,w) gives -eta(t w,w) = t b^2 = (t b) b. Clause (iv) applies (i)-(ii) to -v,-w, using that the negative of a past timelike vector is future timelike (def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). No step uses the Axiom of Choice: the frame is finite-dimensional and the only inequality is the finite-sum Cauchy-Schwarz theorem.

items.title: The reversed triangle inequality and convexity of the future timelike cone
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Sum of two future timelike vectors. If v,w in V are future timelike then v + w is future timelike and sqrt(-eta(v+w,v+w)) >= sqrt(-eta(v,v)) + sqrt(-eta(w,w)), with equality if and only if v and w are positive proportional. (b) Convexity and concavity along segments. If v,w are future timelike then t v + (1-t) w is future timelike for every real t in [0,1], so the future timelike set is convex; moreover sqrt(-eta(t v + (1-t) w, t v + (1-t) w)) >= t sqrt(-eta(v,v)) + (1-t) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) for every t in [0,1], with equality for 0 < t < 1 if and only if v and w are positive proportional. (c) Finite sums. If v_1,...,v_k are future timelike then v_1 + ... + v_k is future timelike and sqrt(-eta(sum_i v_i, sum_i v_i)) >= sum_i sqrt(-eta(v_i,v_i)), with equality if and only if all v_i are positive multiples of one single future timelike vector. The inequalities are those of the model's eta and are independent of any chart; they are the reversed (Lorentzian) forms of the triangle inequality of the spatial Euclidean structure.
items.strategy: Proof from lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors and the coordinate description of the cone. (a) Future direction and timelikeness: in an inertial frame write v = (v^0,v_s), w = (w^0,w_s); the coordinate description of the future cone (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components) gives v^0 > |v_s| and w^0 > |w_s|, so (v+w)^0 = v^0 + w^0 > |v_s| + |w_s| >= |v_s + w_s| by the triangle inequality for the Euclidean norm (cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm), which is exactly the coordinate description of future timelikeness for v + w. Inequality: sqrt(-eta(v+w,v+w))^2 = -eta(v,v) - 2 eta(v,w) - eta(w,w) = a^2 + b^2 + 2(-eta(v,w)) with a := sqrt(-eta(v,v)), b := sqrt(-eta(w,w)); by the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality -eta(v,w) >= ab, so the square is at least (a+b)^2, and monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives (lem-of-square-monotone, thm-of-square-roots) gives the claim. Equality requires -eta(v,w) = ab, which by clause (ii) of the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz lemma is exactly positive proportionality. (b) For 0 <= t <= 1 the vector t v is future timelike when t > 0 (its coordinates are (t v^0, t v_s) with t v^0 > t|v_s| = |t v_s|) and 0 when t = 0; applying (a) to the two future timelike vectors t v and (1-t) w (with the zero vector case handled directly) gives both the membership and the inequality, and the equality statement reduces to the equality case of (a) applied to those two vectors, which are positive proportional exactly when v and w are. (c) Induction on k using (a): thm-induction-principle; the equality case is the conjunction of the equality conditions at each step, which forces all vectors onto one positive ray. All arguments are finite-dimensional and no choice principle is used.

items.title: Existence of an inertial frame whose time axis is a prescribed future timelike direction
items.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let d in V be a future timelike displacement and put T := sqrt(-eta(d,d)) > 0 and n := d/T. Then: (i) eta(n,n) = -1 and n is future timelike, so n is a future unit timelike vector; (ii) for every event o there is an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) of the model with e_0 = n; (iii) for the inertial chart x of any such frame one has x(o + lambda d) = (lambda T, 0, 0, 0) for every real lambda; in particular x(o) = 0 and x(o + d) = (T, 0, 0, 0). Consequently, for any two events p,q with q - p = d, the chart of such a frame represents the displacement q - p by the coordinate vector (T,0,0,0): the spatial coordinates of p and q agree and their time coordinates differ by T.
items.strategy: Proof. (i) Bilinearity gives eta(n,n) = eta(d,d)/T^2 = -1 (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-rational-power), and n is future timelike because the future timelike set is closed under multiplication by the positive real 1/T (cor-sr-reverse-triangle-and-future-cone-convexity, clause (b)). (ii) Fix any inertial frame with origin o, with basis (f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3) (lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist). Let (n^0, n_s) be the coordinates of n in this frame. Since n is future timelike, the coordinate description of the future cone (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components) gives n^0 > |n_s| >= 0, and eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 gives (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0, so the boost parameter beta := n_s/n^0 (a vector of R^3) satisfies |beta| = |n_s|/n^0 < 1 (def-lorentz-boost). Let B := B(beta) be the passive boost of the frame. By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse (iv), B n = f_0; by the same lemma (i) and (iii), B is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse B^{-1} = B(-beta). Define the ordered basis e_0 := n and e_i := B^{-1} f_i for i = 1,2,3; then it is the image under the Lorentz map B^{-1} of the eta-orthonormal basis (f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3) with B^{-1} f_0 = n = e_0, so it is eta-orthonormal with eta(e_0,e_0) = -1 and eta(e_0,e_i) = 0 (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure (i),(iii)); its first vector is future, and it is positively oriented because B^{-1} is proper, hence preserves the oriented volume form and the orientation class (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure (iii)). Therefore (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is an inertial frame with first vector n (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). (iii) For its chart x(p) = E^{-1}(p - o) with E(u) = sum_a u^a e_a one has E(1,0,0,0) = e_0 = n, hence x(o + lambda d) = E^{-1}(lambda d) = lambda T E^{-1}(n) = lambda T (1,0,0,0), and x(o) = 0. No choice principle is used: the construction uses one finite-dimensional basis and the explicit boost of def-lorentz-boost.

items.title: The displacement of a future timelike worldline is future timelike
items.statement:
Let $c>0$ and let $x:[a,b]\to A$ be a future timelike worldline with $a<b$
([[def-interval]]) that is piecewise $C^1$ with partition
$a=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_m=b$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], with future timelike interior
tangents and finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents. Put $p:=x(a)$,
$q:=x(b)$ and $d:=q-p$. Then $d$ is future timelike. More precisely, writing
$\xi^a:=x_A^a\circ x$ for the coordinate path of the chart $x_A$ of any inertial
frame, one has
$$\xi^0(b)-\xi^0(a)>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad|\xi_{\mathrm{vec}}(b)-\xi_{\mathrm{vec}}(a)|<\xi^0(b)-\xi^0(a),$$
where $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean spatial norm of
[[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]. Consequently $p\ne q$,
the number $\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}$ is a positive real number, and in every inertial
chart the time component of $d$ is positive and dominates the Euclidean norm of
its spatial part, which is exactly the coordinate description of future
timelikeness in that chart. Completeness of the real numbers is inherited
from the improper-integrability supplier; no compactness assumption beyond
the given compact interval or choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Apply lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability in an arbitrary inertial chart xi=(xi0,xi_vec). Finite one-sided quotient derivatives give continuity at the corners; on every compact interior truncation each derivative is continuous and the ordinary FTC applies. The lemma proves absolute improper integrability and the exact finite telescoping endpoint increments. Since every interior tangent is future timelike, xi0'-|xi_vec'|>0 throughout each open piece. It is continuous and positive on a compact interior neighborhood, giving a positive integral there; the rest contributes nonnegatively. The improper vector norm inequality proved by truncation gives |xi_vec(b)-xi_vec(a)|<=sum_i integral |xi_vec'|<sum_i integral xi0'=xi0(b)-xi0(a). Therefore the displacement is future timelike and nonzero in the arbitrary frame, its Lorentz norm gives a strictly positive square root, and all claimed coordinate inequalities follow. No continuous extension of the derivative, closed-piece Riemann integrability, or (H) is used; the former (H) cases remain included.

items.title: The endpoint bound for proper time and the maximality of the straight worldline in affine Minkowski space
items.statement:
Let $c>0$ and let $x:[a,b]\to A$ be a future timelike worldline with $a<b$
([[def-interval]]) that is piecewise $C^1$ with partition
$a=s_0<s_1<\dots<s_m=b$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], with total proper time
$\Delta\tau(x)$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]. Put $p:=x(a)$, $q:=x(b)$
and $T:=\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$, a positive real number
([[lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline]]). Then:

**(i) Endpoint bound.** $c\,\Delta\tau(x)\le T$.

**(ii) Equality case.** $c\,\Delta\tau(x)=T$ if and only if $x$ is a strictly
increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from $p$ to $q$: there is a
continuous strictly increasing surjection $\sigma:[a,b]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(a)=0$, $\sigma(b)=1$, $C^1$ on every open piece of a finite weak
piecewise partition of $[a,b]$, with $\sigma'(s)>0$ at every point of each open
piece and finite positive one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both
endpoints of every piece, without any requirement that $\sigma'$ extend
continuously there, such that $x(s)=p+\sigma(s)(q-p)$ for every $s\in[a,b]$;
equivalently, every open-piece tangent $x'(s)$ is a positive multiple of
$q-p$.

**(iii) Strictness.** If the image of $x$ is not contained in the straight
segment $\{p+\lambda(q-p):0\le\lambda\le1\}$, then $c\,\Delta\tau(x)<T$. In
particular, if $x$ is piecewise inertial and its piece tangents $d_1,\dots,d_m$
are not all positive multiples of one another (equivalently, its image is not
contained in the straight segment), then the inequality is strict, while a
piecewise inertial itinerary whose piece tangents are all positive multiples of
one another has the straight segment as image and attains the bound.

**(iv) Straight worldlines attain the bound.** For the worldline
$x_s(s):=p+\frac{s-a}{b-a}(q-p)$ one has $c\,\Delta\tau(x_s)=T$; more generally
every worldline whose image is the straight segment and which is traversed in
the future direction attains the bound.

**(v) Scope.** The theorem concerns the affine Minkowski model with a fixed
positive constant $c$; it is a statement about the weak piecewise $C^1$ future
timelike class, including the ordinary Riemann special case (H); it does not
identify proper time with any clock reading, and it asserts nothing about
maximality of geodesics in curved spacetimes or in Lorentzian manifolds with
different global structure.
items.strategy: By lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline, d=q-p is future timelike and T=sqrt(-eta(d,d))>0. Choose the rest inertial frame with e0=d/T by lem-sr-rest-frame-of-a-future-timelike-displacement; the coordinate endpoint increment is (T,0,0,0). On each open piece xi=(xi0,z) has xi0'>|z'|. Put f=sqrt((xi0')^2-|z'|^2) and h=xi0'-f>=0. The integrability lemma gives finite improper integrals of xi0', f and h, the exact coordinate endpoint increment, and subdivision additivity. Hence c Delta tau=sum_i integral f<=sum_i integral xi0'=T. For equality the finite nonnegative sum of integrals h is zero, so every such integral is zero. If h were positive anywhere in an open piece, continuity would give a compact interior neighborhood of positive integral, contradiction. Therefore z'=0 inside every piece. The zero-derivative theorem and continuity at the corners make z constant throughout, while xi0'>0 implies strict time increase. Set sigma(s)=(xi0(s)-xi0(a))/T. Then sigma is continuous, strictly increasing, onto [0,1], C1 with positive derivative on every open piece, and has finite positive one-sided quotient derivatives at the corners because x does and those tangents now lie along d. This gives x=p+sigma d. Conversely that displayed weak parametrization has density T sigma' and the integrability lemma gives sum_i integral sigma'=sigma(b)-sigma(a)=1, attaining T. This proves (i)-(ii). Clause (iii) follows because a history outside the straight segment fails the equality case; for piecewise inertial histories the constant tangents are all positive multiples exactly when all legs have the same future line, and then the image is the full endpoint segment. Clause (iv) is the constant derivative d/(b-a) calculation or the equality case with affine sigma. Clause (v) preserves purely affine mathematical scope and all prior (H) special cases; no clock reading, curved-spacetime maximality or choice principle is introduced.

items.title: Same-endpoint clock comparison: the inertial clock ages most
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions the postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]],
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]], and let $c$ and the SI
conventions be those of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $p$
and $q$ be events with $q-p$ future timelike, fix reals $a<b$, and put
$T:=\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}>0$, and let $x_s:[a,b]\to A$ be the straight
(inertial) future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$,
$x_s(s):=p+\frac{s-a}{b-a}(q-p)$. Let $x:[a,b]\to A$ be a piecewise $C^1$
future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$ in the weak sense of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], with total proper time
$\Delta\tau(x)$ defined by [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]. Then, as
conditional statements about ideal clocks of the adopted model and not about any
actual apparatus:

**(i)** An ideal clock carried along $x_s$ from $p$ to $q$ reads between the
parameter values $a$ and $b$ the time $c^{-1}T$.

**(ii)** An ideal clock carried along $x$ from $p$ to $q$ reads $\Delta\tau(x)$,
and $\Delta\tau(x)\le c^{-1}T$, with equality if and only if $x$ is a strictly
increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from $p$ to $q$ in the
sense of [[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] (ii).

**(iii)** If $x$ is piecewise inertial
([[def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline]]) and its image is not
contained in the straight segment from $p$ to $q$, then
$\Delta\tau(x)<c^{-1}T$ strictly; so among ideal clocks carried between the same
two events along future timelike piecewise $C^1$ histories of the weak class of
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (including its ordinary Riemann
special case (H)) the straight inertial clock records the largest reading, and
every history whose image is not the straight segment records a strictly
smaller one.

**(iv)** The two numbers $\Delta\tau(x)$ and $c^{-1}T$ are determined by the
parametrized histories and the model's conversion constant alone: the integrand
$\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]] involves no chart, so
the comparison is a definite pair of clock readings attached to the same pair of
endpoint events and involves no simultaneity convention.

**Scope and qualification.** The statement inherits the idealizations of its
postulates (ideal pointlike clocks with no acceleration-dependent reading term,
prescribed histories, flat classical spacetime, the fixed conversion constant
$c$); it asserts no measurement outcome, contains no statistical inference, and
carries no claim that real clocks or the physical world are exactly described by
the model. The conclusion is conditional on the named postulates and does not
follow from the geometry alone.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted postulates; the mathematical engine is the weak-class thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum, whose endpoint FTC and equality argument use the local causal integrability supplier. All former (H) histories remain included. (i) The straight history has constant tangent (q-p)/(b-a), so its proper-time function has the constant rate c^{-1} T/(b-a) (def-sr-proper-time straight-segment value) and the clock hypothesis of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light identifies the reading with that integral, giving c^{-1} T. (ii) For a piecewise C^1 history with finitely many kinks the reading is the total proper time of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time (post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis (ii) states the clock hypothesis for exactly this class, referring to the piecewise integral, and post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light fixes the reading for smooth restrictions and the extended clock formulation identifies the finite improper-piece sum); the bound, equality case and strictness are clauses (i)-(iii) of thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum. (iii) A piecewise inertial itinerary with pieces not all in one direction has an image that is not contained in the straight segment from p to q: the image of a straight segment is a straight set, while the itinerary contains its corner event, which is an event of a piece's line not on the other piece's line; hence the strict case of the theorem applies. (iv) The proper-time integrand is built from eta and the tangent alone, so no chart enters either number. Scope obligations: repeat the idealizations and the conditionality in the conclusion; do not upgrade the conditional statement to a claim about real clocks, and do not attach any empirical or statistical content; no experiment is cited and none can strengthen the deduction. No choice principle beyond the published suppliers is used.

items.title: The piecewise inertial twin reunion: conditional differential aging
items.statement: Thought experiment: the piecewise inertial twin reunion of the adopted model, with its conditional conclusion. Adopt post-sr-inertial-covariance, post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis, and let c and the SI conventions be those of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Fix an inertial frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) with chart x, a duration T > 0 in seconds and a speed v with 0 < |v| < c; put gamma := (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}. Define two histories (coordinate time t in seconds, space and time coordinates in metres with x^0 = c t): (stay-at-home) x_stay(t) := x^{-1}(c t, 0, 0, 0) for t in [0, 2T]; (traveler) x_travel(t) := x^{-1}(c t, v t, 0, 0) for t in [0, T] and x_travel(t) := x^{-1}(c t, v(2T - t), 0, 0) for t in [T, 2T]. Then: (i) x_stay is the inertial future timelike worldline from p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0) to q := x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0), and x_travel is a piecewise inertial future timelike worldline from p to q whose two pieces have the constant tangents (c, v, 0, 0) and (c, -v, 0, 0), with the corner r := x^{-1}(cT, vT, 0, 0); the image of x_travel contains the three events p, r, q, which are not collinear in the affine model, so the image of x_travel is not contained in the straight segment from p to q. (ii) Conditional on the postulates, an ideal clock carried from p to q along x_stay reads 2T, while an ideal clock carried from p to q along x_travel reads 2T/gamma = 2T sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2); hence at the reunion event q the traveling clock is behind the stay-at-home clock by 2T(1 - 1/gamma) = 2T(1 - sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2)) > 0. (iii) The conclusion is a comparison of two clock readings at the common events p and q; it does not depend on a simultaneity convention or on the inertial frame used to describe the histories, because both readings are proper-time integrals of the two histories. (iv) Scope and idealization: the scenario is a conditional model statement; the instantaneous turn at r idealizes a turnaround of finite duration, the clocks are ideal with no acceleration-dependent reading term, spacetime is flat, and no gravitational, quantum, apparatus or statistical effect is modeled; no measurement is reported. The conclusion is conditional on the adopted postulates and does not assert that nature is exactly described by the model.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction with the two explicit histories as witnesses. Step (i): differentiate the coordinate formulas; the coordinate derivatives are (c,0,0,0), (c,v,0,0) and (c,-v,0,0) respectively; each has -eta equal to c^2, c^2 - v^2, c^2 - v^2, all positive, and positive time component, so each piece is future timelike (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart); hence x_stay is inertial and x_travel is piecewise inertial in the sense of def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline with corner r, and both are worldlines through p and q. Non-collinearity: p, r, q have coordinate vectors (0,0,0,0), (cT,vT,0,0), (2cT,0,0,0); since vT is nonzero, r is not on the affine line through p and q (whose second coordinate is 0), so the three are not collinear and the image of x_travel is not contained in the straight segment (an affine line maps to an affine line under the chart, so collinearity is exactly collinearity of the coordinate vectors). Step (ii): the straight history has displacement q - p with coordinates (2cT,0,0,0) and -eta(q-p,q-p) = 4c^2T^2, so its reading is c^{-1} 2cT = 2T (def-sr-proper-time straight-segment value and the clock hypothesis of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light); each leg of x_travel has a constant tangent with -eta = c^2(1 - v^2/c^2) = c^2/gamma^2, so its proper time is T/gamma by the same straight-segment value applied to the leg restricted to its closed parameter interval, and the two-leg total is 2T/gamma by the constant-tangent special case (v) and concatenation additivity (vi) of the extended def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Constant leg derivatives satisfy (H), so these improper values are the same ordinary Riemann values; the clock hypothesis of post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis (ii) identifies the reading with this total proper time. The comparison 2T/gamma < 2T for v nonzero is the strict case of pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison (iii), whose equality case is excluded by the non-collinearity of step (i); it can also be read off directly since 0 < 1 - 1/gamma. Step (iii): both readings are given by proper-time integrals built from eta and the tangents alone, so no chart or simultaneity convention enters; the events p and q are common to the two histories. Step (iv): record the idealizations and the conditionality; do not infer any measured outcome, and do not upgrade the statement to a claim about real clocks.

items.title: Acceleration is not an aging term, and the twin comparison is not symmetric: scope caveats
items.statement:
## Scope caveats for the twin reunion

This remark delimits the interpretation of the proper-time comparison of the
twin reunion ([[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]]) in the adopted model, with the ideal clock assumptions of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] and the SI conventions of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. It proves nothing new; it
records what the earlier items do and do not assert.

## Acceleration is not an additional aging term

In the model the reading of an ideal clock between two events of its history is
the proper-time integral of its worldline, by clause (i) of
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for $C^1$ histories and by clause (ii) of
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] for the weak piecewise $C^1$
class ([[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]); no term depending on the
four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]) or on any
higher derivative of the history appears, and the clock hypothesis is precisely
the exclusion of such terms. The corner of the piecewise inertial history is an
idealization: a physical turnaround occupies a finite parameter interval, the
worldline is then $C^1$ or smooth there, and its proper time is still the
integral. The endpoint bound and strictness clause of
[[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] apply to every weak
piecewise future timelike history with the same endpoints $p,q$. Thus any
smoothing of the corner that remains in that class, preserves $p,q$, and
retains at least one event outside the straight segment still gives a strictly
smaller reading than the stay-at-home clock. No existence or convergence
claim for a smoothing family, or equality with the sharp-turn value
$2T/\gamma$, is asserted.

## The comparison is not symmetric in the model

One history of the reunion is the straight segment from $p$ to $q$; the other
contains the corner event $r$ of [[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], and
the three events $p,r,q$ are not collinear: in the chart of that item their
coordinate columns are $(0,0,0,0)$, $(cT,vT,0,0)$ and $(2cT,0,0,0)$ with
$vT\ne0$. Every change of inertial chart is an affine bijection
([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]) and maps collinear
triples to collinear triples, so no change of inertial frame maps the image of
the stay-at-home history onto the image of the traveler's history, nor fixes both
endpoints and exchanges the two histories. The two twins are therefore not
related by an inertial change of description, and the difference of readings is
a model consequence of the different histories, not a consequence of who is
'really moving': the symmetric time-dilation relation of
[[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i) concerns the two frames,
while the reunion comparison concerns the two clock readings at the single
common event $q$.

## Synchronization bookkeeping at the turn

In each momentary inertial rest frame of the traveler the stay-at-home clock runs
slow by the factor $1/\gamma$, and the traveler may legitimately apply the
time-dilation relation using successive pairs of simultaneous events, one
on each clock history in that momentary frame ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i),
[[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]). But the two legs use different
inertial frames. With $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and the turn event $r$ of
[[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], choose both rest-frame charts with origin $p$ as in
[[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]]; the outbound chart
$x'$ then satisfies $x'^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0-\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, so its slice through
$r$ has $x'^0=\gamma cT(1-v^2/c^2)=cT/\gamma$ and meets the stay-at-home
worldline $x^1=0$ at $x^0=\frac{1}{\gamma}\cdot\frac{cT}{\gamma}=cT(1-v^2/c^2)$,
that is at coordinate time $t=T(1-v^2/c^2)=T/\gamma^2$; the inbound rest frame's
chart $x''$ satisfies $x''^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0+\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, and its slice
through $r$ meets the same worldline at $x^0=cT(1+v^2/c^2)$, that is at
coordinate time $t=T(1+v^2/c^2)$. The two slices differ by
$2Tv^2/c^2$ in coordinate time, and the identity
$$2T=\frac{T}{\gamma^2}+\frac{2Tv^2}{c^2}+\frac{T}{\gamma^2},$$
which only uses $1/\gamma^2=1-v^2/c^2$, inserts this gap into the traveler's two
leg-by-leg accounts and reproduces the stay-at-home reading $2T$ at the reunion,
in agreement with the conditional comparison result
[[pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison]]. The naive reciprocity statement
'each twin judges the other's clock to run slow' therefore compares different
pairs of events for the two travelers — events simultaneous in different
momentary frames — and does not apply to the reunion comparison, which concerns
the two clock readings at the single common event $q$.

## Empirical qualification

Everything above is a conditional statement about ideal clocks in the adopted
model: the clocks are ideal with no acceleration-dependent reading term, the
histories are prescribed, spacetime is flat and $c$ is fixed
([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]],
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]). No measurement, apparatus, calibration,
sampling or uncertainty model is involved, and no claim is made about real
clocks or about nature; real clock comparisons would additionally require
apparatus and uncertainty analysis and are outside this remark.
items.strategy: A remark: it delimits the scope and interpretation of the pair's conditional results and supplies no proof obligations. Obligations of precision: (1) records that the model's reading rule has no acceleration term (the cited postulate clauses), that the corner is an idealization, and that the endpoint bound survives the smoothing of the corner; (2) verifies the asymmetry claim with the chart-transition supplier: inertial chart transitions are affine (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), affine maps send collinear triples to collinear triples, and p, r, q are not collinear by the coordinate computation of the thought experiment, so no affine transition takes one image onto the other; (3) computes the two simultaneity slices with the boost formula of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas inside the notation of the thought experiment: the outbound chart x' with x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - (v/c)x^1) assigns to the turn event r the time coordinate gamma cT(1 - v^2/c^2), so its slice x'^0 = const meets the stay-at-home worldline x^1 = 0 at x^0 = cT(1 - v^2/c^2), and the inbound chart x'' with x''^0 = gamma(x^0 + (v/c)x^1) gives x^0 = cT(1 + v^2/c^2); both events are on the stay-at-home worldline whose clock reads coordinate time, so the two assignments differ by 2Tv^2/c^2; the reconciliation arithmetic is 2T = T(1 - v^2/c^2) + 2Tv^2/c^2 + T(1 - v^2/c^2) = 2T/gamma^2 + 2T(1 - 1/gamma^2); (4) restates the absence of empirical content. The remark cites only quantified suppliers for its numerical claims and marks every statement about real apparatus as outside the model. The broadened endpoint bound still applies to every stated smooth or piecewise inertial turnaround; the existing clock assumptions, simultaneity numbers and empirical exclusions are unchanged. The proper-time reference now resolves to the earlier weak-piecewise definition, with constant-tangent legs as its (H) special case.

items.title: Worked reverse Cauchy-Schwarz and reverse triangle inequalities
items.statement: Worked computation in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1). (a) For v := (5,3,0,0) and w := (5,-3,0,0): eta(v,v) = -25 + 9 = -16 and eta(w,w) = -16, so the timelike lengths are sqrt(16) = 4; eta(v,w) = -25 - 9 = -34, so -eta(v,w) = 34 >= 4*4 = 16, and the inequality is strict because v and w are not proportional. (b) For w' := 2v = (10,6,0,0): eta(w',w') = -100 + 36 = -64, sqrt(-eta(w',w')) = 8, eta(v,w') = -50 + 18 = -32 (twice eta(v,v) = -16), and -eta(v,w') = 32 = 4*8, the equality case of the reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the positive proportional pair (v, 2v). (c) Reverse triangle: v + w = (10,0,0,0) has -eta(v+w,v+w) = 100, so sqrt = 10 >= 4 + 4 = 8, again strict since v and w are not proportional. For u := (5,0,0,0), of timelike length 5, one has -eta(v,u) = 25 >= 4*5 = 20 and v + u = (10,3,0,0) with sqrt(-eta(v+u,v+u)) = sqrt(100-9) = sqrt(91) >= 4 + 5 = 9. (d) The two vectors v and w are both future timelike (5 > 3 and 5 > 3 in the first coordinate), so all inequalities are instances of the future timelike hypotheses.
items.strategy: Every line is a finite evaluation of the displayed diagonal form: squares of the coordinate entries, the diagonal metric, and a comparison of exact integers or of the square root of 91 with 9 (via 91 > 81 and monotonicity of the square root). The equality check evaluates -eta(v,2v) = 8^2 - 4^2 + ... directly: -eta(v,2v) = 2*16 = 32 = 4*8. No limiting, continuity or choice argument occurs.

items.title: Worked two-leg itinerary against the straight clock at speed 3c/5
items.statement:
Worked computation in the inertial chart $x$ with metric
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Fix a real $c>0$. Let $T>0$, let $v$ with $0<|v|<c$ and put
$\gamma:=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; let $p:=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$,
$r:=x^{-1}(cT,vT,0,0)$ and $q:=x^{-1}(2cT,0,0,0)$, the parameter in each
coordinate being the laboratory time $t$ in seconds, so that the coordinate
columns displayed are those of the events in the chart with $x^0=ct$.

**(a)** The straight worldline from $p$ to $q$ has displacement
$d:=(2cT,0,0,0)$, with $-\eta(d,d)=4c^2T^2$ and elapsed proper time
$c^{-1}2cT=2T$.

**(b)** The two-leg itinerary $p\to r\to q$, with the parameter on each leg in
$[0,T]$, has first-leg displacement $(cT,vT,0,0)$ with
$-\eta=c^2T^2(1-v^2/c^2)$, hence proper time
$c^{-1}cT\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}=T/\gamma$, and second-leg displacement
$(cT,-vT,0,0)$ with the same value; its two-leg total proper time is
$2T/\gamma$.

**(c)** Comparison: $2T/\gamma<2T$ for every $v$ with $0<|v|<c$, in agreement
with the endpoint bound and with its strictness clause, since the image of the
two-leg itinerary contains the event $r$, which is not on the straight segment
from $p$ to $q$. Numerical specialization $v=3c/5$ (so $\gamma=5/4$): the
readings are $8T/5$ and $2T$, with difference $2T/5$.

**(d)** Equality without affine parametrization: on $[0,1]$ let
$\mu(s):=(s^2+s)/2$, a strictly increasing $C^1$ surjection of $[0,1]$ onto
itself with $\mu'(s)=s+1/2>0$; the worldline
$y(s):=x^{-1}(2cT\mu(s),0,0,0)$ has the straight segment $pq$ as image and
elapsed proper time $c^{-1}\int_0^1 2cT\mu'(s)\,\mathrm ds=2T$: equality in the
endpoint bound does not require the affine parametrization, only a
future-directed strictly increasing one.
items.strategy: Finite computations from the definitions: the displacements are read off the coordinate formulas, -eta is the diagonal quadratic form, and each straight leg's proper time is the straight-segment value of def-sr-proper-time; the two-leg total is the sum of the two leg values by def-sr-piecewise-proper-time (v). The strict comparison uses 1/gamma < 1 and the strictness clause of the endpoint bound. In (d) the tangent is y'(s) = 2cT mu'(s) e_0 with positive coefficient, so the length integrand is 2cT mu'(s) and the integral over [0,1] evaluates to 2cT(mu(1) - mu(0)) = 2cT = 2T after division by c. All numbers are exact rationals in the specialization v = 3c/5.

items.title: Worked simultaneity gap of the traveler's two momentary rest frames at the turn
items.statement:
Fix reals $c>0$, $T>0$, $v=3c/5$ and $\gamma=5/4$.
This is a mathematical proper-time computation: the inertial chart $x$ has metric
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $x^0=ct$; the stay-at-home worldline is
$y_{\mathrm{stay}}(t)=x^{-1}(ct,0,0,0)$ for $t\in[0,2T]$;
the traveler is $y_{\mathrm{travel}}(t)=x^{-1}(ct,vt,0,0)$ on $[0,T]$
and $y_{\mathrm{travel}}(t)=x^{-1}(ct,v(2T-t),0,0)$ on $[T,2T]$.
All clock readings below mean the based mathematical proper-time values
of these curves, initialized to zero at $t=0$
([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]),
so the stay-at-home reading equals $t$; the turn event is
$r:=x^{-1}(cT,3cT/5,0,0)$; the two momentary inertial rest frames of the
traveler are the charts $x'$ and $x''$ of the boosts with velocities $+3c/5$ and
$-3c/5$, both with the same origin $p=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$ as $x$.
Explicitly their bases are $e'_a=B(-\frac35e_1)e_a$ and
$e''_a=B(\frac35e_1)e_a$ for $a=0,1,2,3$; the two charts
are defined from these bases and origin by [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]].

**(a) Outbound rest frame.** The chart $x'$ has
$x'^0=\frac54\bigl(x^0-\frac35x^1\bigr)$; at $r$ this is
$\frac54\bigl(cT-\frac35\cdot\frac{3cT}{5}\bigr)
=\frac54\bigl(cT-\frac{9cT}{25}\bigr)=\frac54\cdot\frac{16cT}{25}=\frac{4cT}{5}$,
so the slice $x'^0=\frac{4cT}{5}$ through $r$ meets the stay-at-home worldline
$x^1=0$ at $\frac54x^0=\frac{4cT}{5}$, that is $x^0=\frac{16cT}{25}$, i.e.
coordinate time $t=\frac{16T}{25}=T\bigl(1-\frac{9}{25}\bigr)$.

**(b) Inbound rest frame.** The chart $x''$ has
$x''^0=\frac54\bigl(x^0+\frac35x^1\bigr)$; at $r$ this is
$\frac54\bigl(cT+\frac{9cT}{25}\bigr)=\frac54\cdot\frac{34cT}{25}
=\frac{17cT}{10}$, so the slice $x''^0=\frac{17cT}{10}$ through $r$ meets the
stay-at-home worldline at $\frac54x^0=\frac{17cT}{10}$, that is
$x^0=\frac{34cT}{25}$, i.e. coordinate time $t=\frac{34T}{25}
=T\bigl(1+\frac{9}{25}\bigr)$.

**(c) The gap.** The two momentary frames assign to the stay-at-home clock
'at the time of the turn' the two different readings $\frac{16T}{25}$ and
$\frac{34T}{25}$; their difference is $\frac{18T}{25}=\frac{2Tv^2}{c^2}$, the
simultaneity gap.

**(d) Reconciliation.** The traveler's own clock reads $\frac45T=\frac{20T}{25}$
at the turn and $\frac85T=\frac{40T}{25}$ at the reunion; during each leg his
momentary frame assigns to the stay-at-home clock the advance
$\frac{16T}{25}$ (outbound from $0$ to $\frac{16T}{25}$; inbound from
$\frac{34T}{25}$ to $2T=\frac{50T}{25}$); with the gap $\frac{18T}{25}$ the total
assignment is $\frac{16T}{25}+\frac{18T}{25}+\frac{16T}{25}=\frac{50T}{25}=2T$,
the stay-at-home reading at the reunion, while the traveler reads
$\frac85T=\frac{40T}{25}$; the two readings differ by $\frac{2T}{5}
=\frac{10T}{25}$.

**(e) The two rest frames are distinct.** Their relative boost parameter is the
collinear composition
$\frac{2\cdot(3/5)}{1+9/25}=\frac{6/5}{34/25}=\frac{15}{17}\ne0$, so the
traveler's momentary inertial frame changes at the turn.
items.strategy: Direct substitution into the boost transition formula of lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas: each slice computation is a linear equation in x^0 along x^1 = 0; the arithmetic is exact with gamma = 5/4 and beta = 3/5. The relative boost parameter of the two frames is the collinear composition of lem-sr-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition (a boost of 3/5 followed by a boost of -3/5 in the composed description gives 2*(3/5)/(1 + (3/5)^2)). The reconciliation is an addition of the four exact rationals listed. All quantities are evaluations of the model's definitions, not new claims.

items.title: Counterexample: the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality fails outside same-orientation timelike pairs
items.statement: Statement refuted: 'the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality -eta(v,w) >= sqrt(-eta(v,v)) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) holds for every pair of vectors v,w that are individually timelike, regardless of their time orientations, and the analogous reversed form |eta(v,w)| >= sqrt(eta(v,v)) sqrt(eta(w,w)) holds for every pair of spacelike vectors'. First witness: in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1) let v := (5,3,0,0), future timelike with -eta(v,v) = 16, and w := (-5,3,0,0), past timelike with -eta(w,w) = 16. Then eta(v,w) = 25 + 9 = 34 > 0, so -eta(v,w) = -34, while sqrt(-eta(v,v)) sqrt(-eta(w,w)) = 16; the asserted inequality -34 >= 16 is false. The sum v + w = (0,6,0,0) is spacelike (eta(v+w,v+w) = 36 > 0), so the failure is exactly the failure of the future cone to contain sums of vectors of opposite orientation. Second witness: v := (0,1,0,0) and w := (0,1,1,0) are spacelike with eta(v,v) = 1, eta(w,w) = 2 and eta(v,w) = 1, so |eta(v,w)| = 1 < sqrt(2) = sqrt(eta(v,v)) sqrt(eta(w,w)): the reversed spacelike form fails for a pair whose span contains no null direction. Hence the same-orientation timelike hypothesis of lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors cannot be dropped, and the spacelike reversed inequality is not universal.
items.strategy: Both witnesses are finite evaluations of the diagonal form: eta(v,w) for the mixed-orientation pair, eta(v+w,v+w), and the spacelike quantities are computed by direct multiplication and addition; the comparisons 34 > 16 and 1 < sqrt(2) are exact (squaring the second). The examples make no claim beyond the failure of the stated universal quantifiers; the positive results are lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors (same-orientation future timelike pairs) and its past-timelike clause.

items.title: Counterexample: attainment of the endpoint bound does not force the future time orientation
items.statement:
The following claim is false: if a piecewise $C^1$ curve
$x:[\alpha,\beta]\to A$ with nonzero timelike tangents runs from an event $p$ to
an event $q$ and attains the endpoint bound
$\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ in the length-integral sense, that is
$\int_\alpha^\beta\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,\mathrm ds=\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$, then
its tangents must be future timelike, so that $x$ is a worldline of the model.

Counterexample: in the inertial chart $\xi$ with diagonal metric
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ let $d:=(5,3,0,0)$, a future timelike
displacement with $\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}=4$, and put
$p:=\xi^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$, $q:=\xi^{-1}(-5,-3,0,0)=p-d$ and $x(s):=p-s\,d$ for
$s\in[0,1]$. Then $x(0)=p$, $x(1)=p-d=q$, and $x'(s)=-d$ is past timelike for
every $s$, so $x$ is not a future timelike worldline; but its length integrand
is $\sqrt{-\eta(-d,-d)}=\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}=4$ and its length integral over
$[0,1]$ equals $4$, while $\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}=\sqrt{-\eta(-d,-d)}=4$: the
bound is attained with equality by a past-directed parametrization. Attainment
of the length bound therefore does not force the future time orientation; the
model's clock interpretation separately restricts its readings to future
timelike worldlines ([[def-sr-proper-time]],
[[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]). Within the future timelike
worldline class the equality case is characterized by
[[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] (ii).
items.strategy: Direct computation: eta(-d,-d) = eta(d,d) = -16, so the integrand is the constant 4 and the integral over [0,1] is 4; q - p = -d has the same timelike length. The counterexample isolates exactly the quantifier that fails (attainment does not imply future-directedness); it does not contradict the endpoint-bound theorem, which is stated for future timelike worldlines, and it records why future orientation is an explicit hypothesis of the model worldline class; it is not forced by numerical length attainment.

items.title: Worked rest frame of the future timelike displacement (5,3,0,0)
items.statement: Worked computation in an inertial frame with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1). Let d := (5,3,0,0), future timelike with -eta(d,d) = 25 - 9 = 16, T := 4 and n := d/T = (5/4,3/4,0,0). (a) n is future unit timelike: eta(n,n) = -25/16 + 9/16 = -1 and n^0 = 5/4 > 3/4 = |n_vec|. (b) The boost parameter beta := n_vec/n^0 = (3/5,0,0) has |beta| = 3/5 < 1 and gamma = 5/4; the passive boost B(beta) of def-lorentz-boost sends n to e_0, as clause (iv) of lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse requires, since gamma(1, 3/5, 0, 0) = (5/4, 3/4, 0, 0) = n. (c) The basis (e'_0, e'_1, e'_2, e'_3) := (n, B(-beta)e_1, B(-beta)e_2, B(-beta)e_3) has coordinate vectors e'_0 = (5/4,3/4,0,0), e'_1 = (3/4,5/4,0,0), e'_2 = (0,0,1,0), e'_3 = (0,0,0,1); the checks eta(e'_0,e'_0) = -1, eta(e'_1,e'_1) = -9/16 + 25/16 = 1, eta(e'_0,e'_1) = -(5/4)(3/4) + (3/4)(5/4) = 0, eta(e'_2,e'_2) = eta(e'_3,e'_3) = 1 and eta(e'_i,e'_j) = 0 for the remaining pairs show that (o;e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3) is an inertial frame with first vector n. (d) Its chart x' assigns to d the coordinates (4,0,0,0): d = 4n = 4 e'_0, so E'^{-1}(d) = (4,0,0,0); in particular the two endpoints of any displacement 4n have equal spatial coordinates in x' and time coordinates differing by 4.
items.strategy: Finite computations: the coordinates of B(-beta)e_1 are obtained from the coordinate action of def-lorentz-boost (x''^0 = gamma(x^0 + beta x^1), x''^1 = gamma(x^1 + beta x^0) at (0,1,0,0)), giving (gamma beta, gamma, 0, 0) = (3/4, 5/4, 0, 0); the orthonormality checks are exact rational evaluations of the diagonal form; and the chart value is the definition x'(p) = E'^{-1}(p - o) with E'(1,0,0,0) = e'_0. The example is the concrete instance of lem-sr-rest-frame-of-a-future-timelike-displacement.
